Brand launch

Bro Seltzer

A low-calorie hard seltzer, launched from home during lockdown. The look mixes vintage portraits with loud modern graphics, so the bottle stands out on a shelf full of safe drinks packaging.

I made the packaging concepts, a colour-coded label for each flavour, T-shirts, standees and the launch posts for each state.

Client
Indospirit
Role
Marketing Executive. Design, content and launch rollout
Year
2020
Made
Labels, pack, merchandise, social campaign, launch collateral

White Rhino Brewing

My entry to White Rhino Brewing Co's label design competition. I called it Brewing Vapourwave. Purple, pink and teal, big type, and a label loud enough to read from across a bar.

BCG Earth Center

BCG was launching its Climate and Sustainability Hub in India. The brief started as an event logo and grew into a full system across brand, digital and print.

Our direction was simple. Localise, don't translate. I developed the Earth Center mark, then carried it through invitations, screens, signage and print for the launch in Gurugram.

Client
Boston Consulting Group
Role
Associate Designer in a team of five. Design lead: Saroj Singh
Year
2022
Award
Silver, Best in Communication, BCG Design Studios Global Awards 2022
Editorial

BCG × Retailers Association of India

BCG and RAI publish a flagship report on Indian retail each year. The 2023 edition looked at how advanced analytics and AI could change the sector.

I led the design. One grid that holds heavy content without tiring the reader, custom isometric illustration for the retail theme, charts that are quick to scan, and 3D illustration to break up long text.

Client
BCG and Retailers Association of India
Role
Lead designer
Year
Published February 2023
Made
Cover, layout system, illustration, data visualisation
Campaign

Woodland × Woods

Woodland is one of India's biggest outdoor footwear brands. Woods is its premium lifestyle label for a younger crowd. I worked inside the marketing team on both.

For Woodland I planned and directed a three-day location shoot in Rishikesh with around 30 pairs of shoes, then built the print ads and social posts from it. For Woods I organised an influencer meet at the brand's store.

Client
Woodland and Woods
Role
Design intern. Shoot direction, ads, social
Year
2019
Illustration system

Indian Bank

Indian Bank was moving customers from the counter to digital, with a new frontline role to help them: the Digital Banking Champion. The bank needed staff to see what that role looks like in a real branch.

I built one cast of characters and one modular branch, then used them across every scenario. Delivered in four days, from brief to final scenes.

Client
Indian Bank, through BCG
Role
Character system, environment design, scene illustration
Year
2023
Visual storytelling

Futures Symposium 2050

A design futures project about care and company for people who live alone in 2050. I told it as a symposium held in that year, through Maya and her robotic assistant Viko.

I designed the full deck, the characters and three signal posters. Character images are composited from stock. Backgrounds were generated with DALL-E.

For
Master of Design, University of Auckland
Role
Individual work. Graded A+
Year
2024
Icon set

Digital Hearing Journeys

A court in Victoria, Australia was moving hearings online. Three very different people use the same portal: a police informant, a person defending themselves, and a civil plaintiff with a lawyer.

I drew one icon and illustration set and reused it across all three journey maps, so the client could read the whole service at a glance.

Client
BCG Australia
Role
Illustration and journey map design
Year
2021

Design that makes hard things easy to read.

I trained in fashion communication at NIFT New Delhi, then learned speed and polish at BCG's global in-house design studio. Nearly three years, more than 1,500 pieces of work, for clients in banking, retail, pharma and energy.

I moved to New Zealand for a Master of Design at the University of Auckland. I finished with First Class Honours, the Distinguished Graduate Award and First in Course.

I like briefs with a real product at the end. A bottle, a report, a launch, a shoot. I can take one from the first sketch to print-ready files.
